The Fear of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and his Weeping Over Worldly Prosperity

Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that some food was once served to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) after he had fasted. He said, "Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) who was a better person than I was martyred and shrouded in a sheet (so small) that would leave his legs exposed when his head was covered, and his head exposed when his feet were covered. Hamza (RA) who was also a better person than I, was also martyred. Thereafter, worldly wealth was spread out before us and we fear that our good deeds may have been rewarded in advance (in this world rather than in the Aakhirah)." He then started weeping so much that he even left his food.[^2]

Hadhrat Naufal bin Ayaadh Hudhali says, "Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) was our companion and an excellent one indeed. He took us home one day and when he entered he first took a bath before sitting down with us. A platter with bread and meat was then served to us. When the platter was put down, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) started to weep. 'What makes you weep, O Abu Muhammad?' we asked. He replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away without him or his family filling their bellies with even barley bread. I do not think that what we have been kept back to enjoy is better than what they had."[^3]
He Asks Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) About Worldly Prosperity and her Reply

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) once went to Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) and asked, "Dear mother! I fear that my wealth will destroy me because I am the wealthiest of the Quraysh." She advised him saying, "Dear son! Then spend (in charity) because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Verily there are some of my companions who will never see me after I part from them.'" Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) then left and happened to meet Hadhrat Umar (RA). When he informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) about what Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) had told him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to her and asked, "I ask you in the name of Allaah to tell me whether I am amongst them."
